status: Synthetic kinematic controls only. These are not reviewed negative recordings and not a false-acceptance rate. Real no-sign and unsupported-sign false acceptance is NOT MEASURED.
source: tests/fixtures/asl-negative-controls.ts through the real recognition worker (tests/asl-negative-controls.test.ts)

explanations.adjusting glasses: Descending from the eyes, the open hand passes the mouth and moves down and sideways. In 2-D landmarks this matches the THANK YOU rule's mouth-departure geometry. Not changed: no reviewed THANK YOU or glasses recordings exist to justify a stricter origin rule, and THANK YOU already abstains on 3/3 development clips.
explanations.pushing hair aside near the forehead: An open hand moving sideways from the forehead matches the HELLO salute geometry. Not changed for the same reason.
explanations.lowering a hand from the mouth to rest: Indistinguishable from THANK YOU in 2-D landmarks without handshape, palm-orientation or contact evidence.
explanations.lifting a fist as if holding a cup: Fixed 2026-10-21: produced SORRY because circularMotion accumulated an arbitrary +/-pi at each crossing of the bounding-box centre by a straight up-and-down path. Loops must now enclose at least 0.3 of their normalized box (an ellipse encloses about 0.785).
explanations.raising an open hand from the chin towar: The HELLO rule checks a raised, mostly open hand sweeping sideways near the head but not the sweep direction, so moving toward the forehead also matches. The salute moves away from the forehead; constraining direction needs reviewed HELLO recordings (HELLO is 1/3 on development clips) to avoid further recall loss.

demo_mitigation: Between signs, rest the hands below the chest or out of frame. Do not touch the face, glasses or hair, do not wave, shield the eyes or blow a kiss during the demonstration. Every confirmed word is labelled as a rule or model match and can be removed.
adversarial_inventory: docs/gitex/adversarial-inventory.json (19 patterns x 36 capture variations through the real worker, tests/asl-adversarial-inventory.test.ts)

adversarial_explanations.adjusting glasses: As above: the descent from the eyes past the mouth matches the THANK YOU mouth-departure geometry under every variation (36/36).
adversarial_explanations.pushing glasses up the nose: Same mechanism as adjusting glasses: an open hand rises to the nose bridge and descends past the mouth, so THANK YOU fires under every variation (36/36).
adversarial_explanations.pushing hair aside near the forehead: As above: a sideways open-hand sweep at forehead height matches HELLO under every variation (36/36).
adversarial_explanations.tucking hair behind the ear: The final sideways sweep at ear height reaches the HELLO travel threshold only at the closer/farther camera distances and at normal or slow speed without dropout (12/36). Fast (x1.4) or dropout runs abstain.
adversarial_explanations.raising an open hand from the chin towar: As above: the HELLO rule does not check sweep direction (36/36).
adversarial_explanations.shielding the eyes from light: The hold at the brow followed by a descent past the mouth matches THANK YOU (28/36). Fast clean or fast dropout runs abstain because the descent is too short-lived.
adversarial_explanations.waving to someone across the room: A raised open hand oscillating sideways near head height is exactly the HELLO rule's geometry (36/36). HELLO is a greeting, so this may be the right word, but the rule cannot tell a wave from the ASL salute.
adversarial_explanations.lowering a hand from the mouth to rest: As above: indistinguishable from THANK YOU in 2-D landmarks (36/36).
adversarial_explanations.blowing a kiss: An open hand leaving the mouth outward and upward matches the HELLO sideways sweep near the head at slow and normal speed (24/36); every fast (x1.4) run abstains.

adversarial_summary: 280 of 684 synthetic runs produced a word: HELLO 144, THANK YOU 136, and nothing else. Face touching, fist lifting, conversation and coughing produced no words under any variation. Mirrored left-handed runs behave exactly like right-handed ones. These are synthetic rule outcomes, not a false-acceptance rate.
